title: Lead investigators on the most industry research money
question: Which San Francisco physicians lead the studies that draw the most research money from manufacturers, and does one company supply most of it?
finding: 701 San Francisco physicians are named as a lead investigator on industry research payments for 2019 to 2025. The largest total is on studies led by Alain Algazi: $119.2 million, Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation (96%), paid to UCSF Medical Center. 9 of the top 60 lead $5 million or more with 90% or more from a single company. 10 lead investigators also appear in the ownership file (Michael Blum: Vital Connect, Inc; Jeffrey Golden: Pulmonx Corporation; Luis Savastano: Endovascular Engineering Inc.; Endovascular Engineering, Inc.). The money goes to the institution, not to the investigator.
how: The same research-payment records, added up by each principal investigator who has a San Francisco address. A payment naming two investigators is counted under both. "Paid to" is the recipient that received most of the money. The last column marks investigators who also hold an ownership interest in the previous screen.
limits: Leading a study that a manufacturer pays for is disclosed. The dollars were paid to the recipient in the "Paid to" column, in nearly every case a hospital or institution and not the investigator, and a total can reflect a single very costly trial. One company supplying nearly all of the money is what a row looks like when the investigator leads that company's trial. Sums across investigators double-count shared studies.
